$description: Every Humanbase API endpoint this front end calls. pnpm api:verify checks each GET example against a target API. pnpm samples:record saves each listed sample as the data shown when the API is off.

usedBy: GeneSearchService.list (lists too long for a URL, such as the Modules example sets)
ModuleService gene names for a result (by Entrez ID)

handBuiltSamples.why: Submitting starts a job, so the submit answer is hand-built and says so in its note field.

recordedByHandSamples.why: Polling is a POST, which pnpm samples:record only sends to read-only endpoints. This poll of the live cache was recorded on October 21, 2026 with every term, so offline term counts match live; only the per-term edge lists are left out, as the note in the file says. The MAGE renal panel (kidney-v3) was recorded the same way on October 23, 2026; submitting it answered 200 with the cached result, so its submit file holds that same body. The renal panel rerun with extended_universe=true (body_tag af5b378…) was polled the same way on October 24, 2026, and both annotation reruns of the renal result (with and without the flag, sending the result's own gene list) were submitted once each that day; each answered 200 with its cached result.

handBuiltSamples.why: Submitting starts a real job, which needs approval, so no submission is recorded. With the API off, submitting the example BMI file to adipose tissue answers with the hand-built running job below; any other submission explains that jobs need the API.

Real NetWAS job c66b3d05 (the documented example, recorded October 20, 2026) is the finished job. The queued, running and failed jobs are still hand-built, shaped like the schema, with IDs that are clearly not real jobs, and say so in their note field. The recorded 404 is the not-found answer.

endpoints.$note: Not the API: the example files the API documents and the results_file a finished job links to, read as text.

handBuiltSamples.why: The result file of real NetWAS job c66b3d05, trimmed to its first 200 ranked genes with the full header; the file says so in its note.

endpoints.$note: Multipart form, read from the live site’s form on October 20, 2026: title, email, input_type (vcf, bed or fasta), ds_model in lower case (sei, beluga or seqweaver; ExPecto and in silico mutagenesis send beluga with expecto or insilico set to true), signup, expecto, insilico and genome_assembly (hg19, or hg38 except for ExPecto). The input goes as upload_file for an uploaded file or upload_textarea for pasted text and examples.

handBuiltSamples.why: Submitting starts a real job. With the API off, submitting a tool’s example answers with a hand-built running job; any other file explains that jobs need the API.

The in silico mutagenesis example job 0576e894-a2c5-48bb-9bdf-227962495d5f, written on the Figma job screens, read on October 20, 2026.

handBuiltSamples.why: Real jobs are recorded for every model (Sei 2e18fedf, Beluga 8b26a498, ExPecto e504e3cc, Seqweaver 76aea8fe, in silico mutagenesis 0576e894). The queued, running and failed states are still hand-built from the Figma screens, with IDs that are clearly not real jobs, and say so in their note.

endpoints.$note: The job page reads every variant in the genome browser’s view, as humanbase.io does. Samples cover each example variant’s opening view, 50 kb either side of it, as humanbase.io opens.

feature_name is the feature’s index in GET /api/deepsea/Beluga/features/ (297 is HepG2 / CEBPB). The body is { positions: ["position,ref,alt,value", ...], percentile: [...] }, three substitutions per base. Samples cover two of the example job’s four sequences for HepG2 / CEBPB, about 120 KB each, written compactly; other choices explain that the sample doesn’t include them.

Sei answers with 4 MB, too large to bundle; its 40 sequence classes are hand-built below. Seqweaver and Beluga are recorded without descriptions. ExPecto reads the same Beluga list with expecto=true and only needs its 218 expecto_features, so that sample drops model_features. sei_hgmd is the Sei HGMD browser’s 40 sequence classes, in its own order.

Precomputed predictions for every variant in a range: the ASD variants on DNA_Binding (2,002 features) and RNA_Binding, and Seqweaver's gnomAD variants with score_type=seqweaver (232 features, each record with its variant_score). Samples round to two decimals: DNA for the default range, CHD8 and SCN2A; RNA for the default range; Seqweaver gnomAD for 2 kb at the default range's center, since the whole 210 kb range is 13.7 MB. sei_hgmd takes no score_type: without a range it returns all 853 HGMD variants for the heatmap, rounded to three decimals as humanbase.io’s tooltip shows them; its range samples are the first variant of each heatmap order, and the third in the dataset’s order, where Next variant first leaves chr17, 50 kb either side.

ExPecto (expecto-tissues) and ExPecto SC (clever-tissues). collapse=true leaves out the 14 tissues marked redundant. A gene without predictions answers 404. Samples are rounded (3 and 2 decimals, beyond what the heatmaps show) to keep them small; CCR1, the second ExPecto example, is 1.6 MB and is not bundled.

Not in /api/schema/ (see the issue for Julien beside the ExPecto lane). The gene filter matches the start of the symbol, so ExpectoService keeps the exact gene. position is ignored; position__gte and position__lte work. 20 rows a page. ASD Browser: labels__name=asd, 20 rows per API page (page_size is ignored); chromosome with position__gte and position__lte limit it to a range. Samples: the first two pages, the default range chr1:2,230,000-2,440,000 (34 variants, two pages) and the CHD8, SCN2A and CHD9 gene spans.
The ASD columns by name, such as DNA Disease impact score and the four junction columns.

geneLookups.$note: Not the API: gene names are looked up in the static files the live genome browser reads on S3 (geneIndex.ix and .ixx, then gencode.bb by transcript). pnpm samples:record saves each listed gene’s span; a name with no file reads as not found while the API is off.

genomeTracks.$note: Not the API: the genome browser reads gene models, scores, segments and sequence from the static track files on S3. pnpm samples:record saves each window padded by its own width on both sides, the listed score files over it (a file with bins, such as per-base conservation, summarised to about that many values), the listed segment files (bigBed, such as GM12878 ChromHMM) over it, and 2 kb of sequence around its center, into genome/tracks.json. The windows from chr1:109792590 on cover the variants whose effects the Seqweaver, Sei, Beluga and ExPecto sample jobs record, with each job's own score files. The windows from chr2:113587327 on, and the gnomAD scores in the chr1:2230000 and CHD8, SCN2A and CHD9 windows, cover the genome browser page (/genome/) for the genes and variants its sample links open: IL1B and ICAM1 in Networks, HNF1B in Modules, IRGM and its rsID results, PTEN, KRT6B in the NetWAS sample, rs531708574 and chr1:877047, with humanbase.io's /genome tracks, gnomAD summarised as conservation is. chr1:2334000-2336000 covers the Seqweaver gnomAD browser's sample view with its gnomAD track; it comes first, so that view reads every gnomAD score rather than a summary. The last three cover the Sei HGMD browser's first variant in each heatmap order, with its sequence class score file.
